- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often overreacts — reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and price is trending downward, model often fails to mean-revert — add 0.5–1.0 price point upward bias to encourage reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment periods — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 price points if sentiment > 0.25 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to correct — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 price points if sentiment drops below -0.25 within 3 days.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is 2–3% below 30-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0 price point to trigger reversion.
